title: Saudi Arabia Reports 1 Fatality, 11 Injured in Latest Attack on Riyadh Airport – Al Jazeera
body:
A projectile struck Saudi Arabia’s King Khalid International Airport on Sunday, killing a Pakistani national and wounding eleven others, the nation’s General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) confirmed. The incident, which unfolded during a busy morning at the Riyadh hub, marks the latest violent episode targeting the kingdom’s critical infrastructure and has prompted heightened security alerts across the country’s aviation network.

The GACA said the explosion occurred near the airport’s western perimeter, where a small, unidentified object detonated on the tarmac. Emergency crews rushed to the scene, evacuating passengers and staff while providing medical aid to the injured. Among the casualties, the deceased was identified as a 32‑year‑old Pakistani expatriate working in the logistics sector. Hospital officials reported that the eleven injured, a mix of airport employees and travelers, suffered from shrapnel wounds and minor burns; all are expected to recover. Saudi authorities have sealed off the affected area and launched a full investigation to determine the source of the projectile and whether it was part of a coordinated attack.

The incident arrives amid a broader pattern of unrest that has increasingly threatened Saudi Arabia’s transport arteries. Over the past year, the kingdom has faced a series of drone and missile strikes on oil facilities, pipelines, and, most recently, a series of low‑altitude incursions targeting the Saudi–Yemen border. While the Houthi movement in Yemen has claimed responsibility for many of those attacks, it has not yet commented on the Riyadh airport event. Analysts suggest that the strike could be an extension of the same campaign, aiming to disrupt the nation’s economic lifelines and signal the reach of militant groups beyond the southern front.

Security experts caution that airports are especially vulnerable because of their high concentration of personnel, equipment, and the symbolic value they carry. “An attack on a major international gateway is designed to sow fear, interrupt commerce, and attract global media attention,” said Dr. Lina Al‑Harthi, a regional security specialist at the Gulf Institute for Strategic Studies. She added that the choice of King Khalid International—one of the kingdom’s busiest airports serving millions of passengers annually—could indicate an escalation in tactics, moving from large‑scale infrastructure to more localized, high‑visibility targets. The incident also raises questions about the effectiveness of Saudi Arabia’s air‑defense shield, which has been credited with intercepting numerous aerial threats in the past year.

In response, the Saudi Ministry of Interior announced the deployment of additional security personnel to all major airports and the activation of a nationwide emergency response protocol. The ministry also called on international partners, including the United States and the United Kingdom, for intelligence sharing to trace the origin of the projectile. Meanwhile, airlines operating out of Riyadh have temporarily rerouted flights and instituted heightened screening procedures, causing minor delays but no major disruptions to the overall flight schedule.

The attack underscores the growing complexity of security challenges facing the kingdom as it seeks to balance rapid economic diversification under Vision 2030 with the need to safeguard its critical infrastructure. As investigations continue, Saudi officials are expected to release a detailed report outlining the findings and any subsequent policy adjustments. The incident serves as a stark reminder that, despite robust defensive measures, the threat landscape remains fluid, and vigilance will be essential to protect both citizens and the nation’s strategic assets in the months ahead.
